title.zh: 卷四十六 志第二十六: 經籍上
title.raw: 卷四十六 志第二十六: 經籍上 Volume 46 Treatises 26: Literature 1

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 46 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: 夫龜文成象，肇八卦於庖犧；

translations.literal: When the tortoise's markings formed images, Fu Xi first traced the Eight Trigrams;
translations.idiomatic: When the tortoise's markings formed images, Fu Xi first traced the Eight Trigrams;

sentences.zh: 鳥跡分形，創六書於蒼頡。

translations.literal: When bird tracks divided into shapes, Cang Jie created the Six Scripts.
translations.idiomatic: When bird tracks divided into shapes, Cang Jie created the Six Scripts.

translations.literal: Sages created and the wise expounded — one source, many streams.
translations.idiomatic: Sages created and the wise expounded — one source, many streams.

sentences.zh: 《墳》《典》起之於前，《詩》《書》繼之於後。

translations.literal: The Canon and the Classic arose first; the Odes and the Documents followed after.
translations.idiomatic: The Canon and the Classic arose first; the Odes and the Documents followed after.

translations.literal: Former kings left their traces; later kings took them as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings left their traces; later kings took them as their measure.

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Observe the patterns of culture to transform the world."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Observe the patterns of culture to transform the world."

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎！」

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: "If a gentleman wishes to transform the people and establish custom, must he not begin with learning!"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: "If a gentleman wishes to transform the people and establish custom, must he not begin with learning!"

translations.literal: Learning is nothing other than what is called written records.
translations.idiomatic: Learning is nothing other than what is called written records.

sentences.zh: 琢玉成器，觀古知今，歷代哲王，莫不崇尚。

translations.literal: Polish jade to make a vessel; observe antiquity to know the present — sage-kings of every age have none failed to honor this.
translations.idiomatic: Polish jade to make a vessel; observe antiquity to know the present — sage-kings of every age have none failed to honor this.

sentences.zh: 自仲尼沒而微言絕，七十子喪而大義乖。

translations.literal: After Confucius died, subtle words ceased; when the seventy disciples passed away, great principles diverged.
translations.idiomatic: After Confucius died, subtle words ceased; when the seventy disciples passed away, great principles diverged.

translations.literal: The house of Qin buried and burned books to keep the common people ignorant;
translations.idiomatic: The house of Qin buried and burned books to keep the common people ignorant;

translations.literal: When Han rose, schools were restored and the Stone Canal established anew.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, schools were restored and the Stone Canal established anew.

sentences.zh: 雄、向校讎于前，馬、鄭討論於後，兩京載籍，由是粲然。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang and Liu Xin collated texts in the earlier age; Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan debated them in the later — the libraries of the two capitals thereby blazed with brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang and Liu Xin collated texts in the earlier age; Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan debated them in the later — the libraries of the two capitals thereby blazed with brilliance.

translations.literal: By the end of Han, when the capital returned westward, more than half were burned or drowned.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Han, when the capital returned westward, more than half were burned or drowned.

sentences.zh: 爰自魏、晉，迄于周、隋，而好事之君，慕古之士，亦未嘗不以圖籍為意也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin down to Zhou and Sui, rulers who loved antiquity and scholars who admired the old likewise never failed to keep written records in mind.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin down to Zhou and Sui, rulers who loved antiquity and scholars who admired the old likewise never failed to keep written records in mind.

translations.literal: Yet north of the Yellow River and south of the Yangtze could not be unified;
translations.idiomatic: Yet north of the Yellow River and south of the Yangtze could not be unified;

translations.literal: regional purchases and compilations left collections still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: regional purchases and compilations left collections still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 而荀勖、李充、王儉、任昉、祖暅，皆達學多聞，曆世整比，群分類聚，遞相祖述。

translations.literal: Yet Xun Xu, Li Chong, Wang Jian, Ren Fang, and Zu Geng were all broadly learned and well informed; generation after generation they arranged and compared, grouped and classified, each following the last.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xun Xu, Li Chong, Wang Jian, Ren Fang, and Zu Geng were all broadly learned and well informed; generation after generation they arranged and compared, grouped and classified, each following the last.

sentences.zh: 或為七錄，或為四部，言其部類，多有所遺。

translations.literal: Some made Seven Records, others Four Divisions — yet in speaking of their categories, much was left out.
translations.idiomatic: Some made Seven Records, others Four Divisions — yet in speaking of their categories, much was left out.

sentences.zh: 及隋氏建邦，寰區一統，煬皇好學，喜聚逸書，而隋世簡編，最為博洽。

translations.literal: When the house of Sui established its state and the realm was unified, Emperor Yang loved learning and delighted in gathering lost books; of Sui's catalogues, none was more comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Sui established its state and the realm was unified, Emperor Yang loved learning and delighted in gathering lost books; of Sui's catalogues, none was more comprehensive.

translations.literal: By the end of the Daye reign, many were lost.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daye reign, many were lost.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，令狐德棻、魏徵相次為秘書監，上言以籍亡逸，請行購募，並奏引學士校定。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Linghu Defen and Wei Zheng in succession served as Director of the Palace Library; they memorialized that because books were lost, purchases should be made, and they also submitted scholars to collate and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, Linghu Defen and Wei Zheng in succession served as Director of the Palace Library; they memorialized that because books were lost, purchases should be made, and they also submitted scholars to collate and fix them.

translations.literal: The corpus of books was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: The corpus of books was fully restored.

sentences.zh: 四部者，甲、乙、丙、丁之次也。

translations.literal: The Four Divisions are ranked Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Divisions are ranked Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 甲部為經，其類十二：一日《易》，以紀陰陽變化。

translations.literal: The Jia division comprises the Classics, with twelve categories: first, the Changes, to record yin-yang transformations.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia division comprises the Classics, with twelve categories: first, the Changes, to record yin-yang transformations.

translations.literal: Second, the Documents, to record the exemplary models of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Documents, to record the exemplary models of emperors and kings.

translations.literal: Third, the Odes, to record rise and decline and songs of praise and lament.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Odes, to record rise and decline and songs of praise and lament.

translations.literal: Fourth, the Rites, to record cultural objects and institutional forms.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the Rites, to record cultural objects and institutional forms.

translations.literal: Fifth, Music, to record sound, appearance, pitch, and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Music, to record sound, appearance, pitch, and measure.

sentences.zh: 六曰《春秋》，以紀行事褒貶。

translations.literal: Sixth, the Spring and Autumn, to record deeds and their praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the Spring and Autumn, to record deeds and their praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 七曰《孝經》，以紀天經地義。

translations.literal: Seventh, the Classic of Filial Piety, to record heaven's norm and earth's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the Classic of Filial Piety, to record heaven's norm and earth's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 八曰《論語》，以紀先聖微言。

translations.literal: Eighth, the Analects, to record the subtle words of the sage.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the Analects, to record the subtle words of the sage.

sentences.zh: 九曰圖緯，以紀六經讖候。

translations.literal: Ninth, charts and weft-texts, to record the prognostications of the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, charts and weft-texts, to record the prognostications of the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 十曰經解，以紀六經讖候。

translations.literal: Tenth, commentaries on the classics, to record exegesis of the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, commentaries on the classics, to record exegesis of the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 十一曰詁訓，以紀六經讖候。

translations.literal: Eleventh, glosses and explanations, to record lexical and semantic study.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, glosses and explanations, to record lexical and semantic study.

sentences.zh: 十二曰小學，以紀字體聲韻。

translations.literal: Twelfth, minor learning, to record character forms and phonology.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, minor learning, to record character forms and phonology.

sentences.zh: 乙部為史，其類十有三：一曰正史，以紀紀傳表志。

translations.literal: The Yi division comprises Histories, with thirteen categories: first, standard histories, to record annals, biographies, tables, and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi division comprises Histories, with thirteen categories: first, standard histories, to record annals, biographies, tables, and treatises.

sentences.zh: 二曰古史，以紀編年系事。

translations.literal: Second, ancient histories, to record events by year.
translations.idiomatic: Second, ancient histories, to record events by year.

sentences.zh: 三曰雜史，以紀異體雜紀。

translations.literal: Third, miscellaneous histories, to record irregular and mixed accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Third, miscellaneous histories, to record irregular and mixed accounts.

sentences.zh: 四曰霸史，以紀偽朝國史。

translations.literal: Fourth, hegemonic histories, to record the state histories of illegitimate dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, hegemonic histories, to record the state histories of illegitimate dynasties.

sentences.zh: 五曰起居注，以紀人君言動。

translations.literal: Fifth, diaries of activity and repose, to record the words and deeds of rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, diaries of activity and repose, to record the words and deeds of rulers.

sentences.zh: 六曰舊事，以紀朝廷政令。

translations.literal: Sixth, old precedents, to record court edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, old precedents, to record court edicts and commands.

sentences.zh: 七曰職官，以紀班序品秩。

translations.literal: Seventh, official posts, to record ranks and grades of office.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, official posts, to record ranks and grades of office.

sentences.zh: 八曰儀注，以紀吉凶行事。

translations.literal: Eighth, ritual protocols, to record auspicious and inauspicious proceedings.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, ritual protocols, to record auspicious and inauspicious proceedings.

sentences.zh: 九曰刑法，以紀律令格式。

translations.literal: Ninth, penal law, to record statutes, commands, formats, and models.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, penal law, to record statutes, commands, formats, and models.

sentences.zh: 十曰雜傳，以紀先聖人物。

translations.literal: Tenth, miscellaneous biographies, to record sages and eminent persons.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, miscellaneous biographies, to record sages and eminent persons.

sentences.zh: 十一曰地理，以紀山川郡國。

translations.literal: Eleventh, geography, to record mountains, rivers, commanderies, and states.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, geography, to record mountains, rivers, commanderies, and states.

sentences.zh: 十二曰譜系，以紀世族繼序。

translations.literal: Twelfth, genealogical registers, to record clans and succession.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, genealogical registers, to record clans and succession.

sentences.zh: 十三曰略錄，以紀史策條目。

translations.literal: Thirteenth, brief catalogues, to record entries in historical compilations.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, brief catalogues, to record entries in historical compilations.

sentences.zh: 丙部為子，其類一十有四：一曰儒家，以紀仁義教化。

translations.literal: The Bing division comprises Masters, with fourteen categories: first, Confucianists, to record benevolence, righteousness, and moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing division comprises Masters, with fourteen categories: first, Confucianists, to record benevolence, righteousness, and moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 二曰道家，以紀清淨無為。

translations.literal: Second, Daoists, to record clarity, stillness, and non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Daoists, to record clarity, stillness, and non-action.

sentences.zh: 三曰法家，以紀刑法典制。

translations.literal: Third, Legalists, to record penal law and institutional codes.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Legalists, to record penal law and institutional codes.

sentences.zh: 四曰名家，以紀循名責實。

translations.literal: Fourth, Logicians, to record aligning names with realities.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Logicians, to record aligning names with realities.

sentences.zh: 五曰墨家，以紀強本節用。

translations.literal: Fifth, Mohists, to record strengthening the root and economizing expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Mohists, to record strengthening the root and economizing expenditure.

sentences.zh: 六曰縱橫家，以紀辯說詭詐。

translations.literal: Sixth, Diplomatists, to record persuasion and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, Diplomatists, to record persuasion and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 七曰雜家，以紀兼敘眾說。

translations.literal: Seventh, Eclectics, to record combined treatment of many schools.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, Eclectics, to record combined treatment of many schools.

sentences.zh: 八曰農家，以紀播植種藝。

translations.literal: Eighth, Agriculturalists, to record planting and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, Agriculturalists, to record planting and cultivation.

sentences.zh: 九曰小說家，以紀芻辭輿誦。

translations.literal: Ninth, fictionists, to record popular sayings and street lore.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, fictionists, to record popular sayings and street lore.

sentences.zh: 十曰兵法，以紀權謀制度。

translations.literal: Tenth, military methods, to record strategy and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, military methods, to record strategy and institutions.

sentences.zh: 十一曰天文，以紀星辰象緯。

translations.literal: Eleventh, astronomy, to record stars, celestial signs, and astrological patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, astronomy, to record stars, celestial signs, and astrological patterns.

sentences.zh: 十二曰歷數，以紀推步氣朔。

translations.literal: Twelfth, calendrical calculation, to record computation of qi and new moons.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, calendrical calculation, to record computation of qi and new moons.

sentences.zh: 十三曰五行，以紀卜筮占候。

translations.literal: Thirteenth, the Five Phases, to record divination and prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, the Five Phases, to record divination and prognostication.

sentences.zh: 十四曰醫方，以紀藥餌針灸。

translations.literal: Fourteenth, medicine, to record drugs, formulas, acupuncture, and moxibustion.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth, medicine, to record drugs, formulas, acupuncture, and moxibustion.

sentences.zh: 丁部為集，其類有三：一曰楚詞，以紀騷人怨刺。

translations.literal: The Ding division comprises Collections, with three categories: first, Songs of Chu, to record the laments of poets.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding division comprises Collections, with three categories: first, Songs of Chu, to record the laments of poets.

sentences.zh: 二曰別集，以紀詞賦雜論。

translations.literal: Second, individual collections, to record rhapsodies, fu, and miscellaneous essays.
translations.idiomatic: Second, individual collections, to record rhapsodies, fu, and miscellaneous essays.

sentences.zh: 三曰總集，以紀文章事類。

translations.literal: Third, general collections, to record writings by subject.
translations.idiomatic: Third, general collections, to record writings by subject.

sentences.zh: 煚等撰集，依班固《藝文志》體例，諸書隨部皆有小序，發明其旨。

translations.literal: Jiong and others compiled their collection following the form of Ban Gu's Bibliographic Treatise; each division's books had small prefaces expounding their purport.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and others compiled their collection following the form of Ban Gu's Bibliographic Treatise; each division's books had small prefaces expounding their purport.

sentences.zh: 近史官撰《隋書經籍志》，其例亦然。

translations.literal: Recently the historiographers compiled the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Sui; the form is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the historiographers compiled the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Sui; the form is the same.

sentences.zh: 竊以紀錄簡編異題，卷部相沿，序述無出前修。

translations.literal: I consider that because records and compilations differ in title and scrolls and divisions follow one another, prefaces and expositions add nothing beyond what earlier editors already wrote.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that because records and compilations differ in title and scrolls and divisions follow one another, prefaces and expositions add nothing beyond what earlier editors already wrote.

sentences.zh: 今之殺青，亦所不取，但紀部帙而已。

translations.literal: In the present green-silk binding we likewise take none of that, but only record divisions and scroll-counts.
translations.idiomatic: In the present green-silk binding we likewise take none of that, but only record divisions and scroll-counts.

sentences.zh: 而煚等所序四部都錄以明新修之旨，今略載之：

translations.literal: Yet the general catalogue of the Four Divisions that Jiong and others prefaced, to clarify the intent of the new compilation, is here briefly set down:
translations.idiomatic: Yet the general catalogue of the Four Divisions that Jiong and others prefaced, to clarify the intent of the new compilation, is here briefly set down:

sentences.zh: 竊以經墳浩廣，史圖紛博，尋覽者莫之能遍，司總者常苦其多，何暇重屋復床，更繁其說？

translations.literal: I consider that the canon is vast and historical charts abundant; those who search cannot cover all, and those who oversee constantly suffer from their multitude — who has leisure to pile bed upon bed and further multiply explanations?
translations.idiomatic: I consider that the canon is vast and historical charts abundant; those who search cannot cover all, and those who oversee constantly suffer from their multitude — who has leisure to pile bed upon bed and further multiply explanations?

sentences.zh: 若先王有闕典，上聖有遺事，邦政所急，儒訓是先，宜垂教以作程，當闡規而開典，則不遑啟處，何獲宴寧。

translations.literal: If former kings left defective canons and supreme sages left unfinished affairs, and state policy urgently requires it while Confucian instruction comes first, then one ought to set teaching as a standard and open the canon by clarifying rules — there would be no leisure to sit at ease; how could one obtain repose?
translations.idiomatic: If former kings left defective canons and supreme sages left unfinished affairs, and state policy urgently requires it while Confucian instruction comes first, then one ought to set teaching as a standard and open the canon by clarifying rules — there would be no leisure to sit at ease; how could one obtain repose?

sentences.zh: 曩之所修，誠惟此義，然禮有未愜，追怨良深。

translations.literal: What was compiled before truly held only this meaning, yet the rites were not fully satisfactory, and regret runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: What was compiled before truly held only this meaning, yet the rites were not fully satisfactory, and regret runs deep.

sentences.zh: 于時秘書省經書，實多亡闕，諸司墳籍，不暇討論。

translations.literal: At the time the Palace Library's classics were in fact much lost or missing, and the archives of the various offices left no leisure for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Palace Library's classics were in fact much lost or missing, and the archives of the various offices left no leisure for discussion.

translations.literal: This was one matter not fully accomplished — the first point.
translations.idiomatic: This was one matter not fully accomplished — the first point.

sentences.zh: 其後周覽人間，頗睹闕文，新集記貞觀之前，永徽已來不取；

translations.literal: Afterward, in touring the realm, missing texts were often seen; the new collection recorded what preceded the Zhenguan era, but nothing since Yonghui was taken;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, in touring the realm, missing texts were often seen; the new collection recorded what preceded the Zhenguan era, but nothing since Yonghui was taken;

sentences.zh: 近書采長安之上，神龍已來未錄。

translations.literal: recent books were gathered only above the Chang'an period; nothing since Shenlong was entered.
translations.idiomatic: recent books were gathered only above the Chang'an period; nothing since Shenlong was entered.

translations.literal: This was a second point where principle was not fully extended.
translations.idiomatic: This was a second point where principle was not fully extended.

sentences.zh: 書閱不遍，事復未周，或不詳名代，或未知部伍。

translations.literal: Books were not fully reviewed, affairs again not fully covered; sometimes names and ages were unclear, sometimes placement in divisions was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Books were not fully reviewed, affairs again not fully covered; sometimes names and ages were unclear, sometimes placement in divisions was unknown.

translations.literal: This was a third point where form was not fully penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: This was a third point where form was not fully penetrated.

sentences.zh: 書多闕目，空張第數，既無篇題，實乖標榜。

translations.literal: Many books lacked entries yet numbers of divisions were listed in vain; without chapter titles, the labels were truly awry.
translations.idiomatic: Many books lacked entries yet numbers of divisions were listed in vain; without chapter titles, the labels were truly awry.

translations.literal: This was a fourth point where the standard was impaired.
translations.idiomatic: This was a fourth point where the standard was impaired.

translations.literal: The prefaces used all drew on Wei the Pure Minister;
translations.idiomatic: The prefaces used all drew on Wei the Pure Minister;

sentences.zh: 所分書類，皆據《隋經籍志》。

translations.literal: the book categories all followed the Bibliographic Treatise of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: the book categories all followed the Bibliographic Treatise of the Sui.

translations.literal: Principle was not fully acceptable; form not fully penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: Principle was not fully acceptable; form not fully penetrated.

translations.literal: This was a fifth point where the facts were not settled.
translations.idiomatic: This was a fifth point where the facts were not settled.

sentences.zh: 昔馬談作《史記》，班彪作《漢書》，皆兩葉而僅成；

translations.literal: Formerly Sima Tan wrote the Records of the Historian and Ban Biao wrote the Book of Han — each barely finished in two generations;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Sima Tan wrote the Records of the Historian and Ban Biao wrote the Book of Han — each barely finished in two generations;

sentences.zh: 劉歆作《七略》，王儉作《七志》，逾二紀而方就。

translations.literal: Liu Xin wrote the Seven Summaries and Wang Jian the Seven Registers — more than two reign-periods passed before they were done.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin wrote the Seven Summaries and Wang Jian the Seven Registers — more than two reign-periods passed before they were done.

sentences.zh: 孰有四萬卷目，二千部書，名目首尾，三年便令終竟，欲求精悉，不其難乎？

translations.literal: Who, then, with forty thousand scroll-titles and two thousand book-divisions, from first entry to last, could finish in three years and still seek precision and completeness — is that not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Who, then, with forty thousand scroll-titles and two thousand book-divisions, from first entry to last, could finish in three years and still seek precision and completeness — is that not difficult?

sentences.zh: 所以常有遺恨，竊思追雪。

translations.literal: Hence regret has always remained; I privately think to make amends.
translations.idiomatic: Hence regret has always remained; I privately think to make amends.

sentences.zh: 乃與類同契，積思潛心，審正舊疑，詳開新制。

translations.literal: Then, sharing purpose with my colleagues, I accumulated thought and applied my mind, examined and corrected old doubts, and opened new standards in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Then, sharing purpose with my colleagues, I accumulated thought and applied my mind, examined and corrected old doubts, and opened new standards in detail.

sentences.zh: 永徽新集，神龍近書，則釋而附也。

translations.literal: The Yonghui new collection and Shenlong recent books were then released and appended.
translations.idiomatic: The Yonghui new collection and Shenlong recent books were then released and appended.

sentences.zh: 未詳名氏，不知部伍，則論而補也。

translations.literal: Where names were unclear and division unknown, discussion supplied the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Where names were unclear and division unknown, discussion supplied the gaps.

translations.literal: Empty listed entries were then found and added upon inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Empty listed entries were then found and added upon inspection.

translations.literal: Unacceptable prefaces were then detailed and separately composed.
translations.idiomatic: Unacceptable prefaces were then detailed and separately composed.

translations.literal: Errors were all corrected; confusion necessarily excised.
translations.idiomatic: Errors were all corrected; confusion necessarily excised.

sentences.zh: 改舊傳之失者三百餘條，加新書之目者六千餘卷。

translations.literal: More than three hundred errors in old transmissions were corrected, and more than six thousand scrolls of new book entries were added.

translations.idiomatic: The Masters register: seventeen categories, 753 titles, 15,637 scrolls.

translations.literal: The Collections register: three categories, eight hundred ninety-two titles, twelve thousand twenty-eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Collections register: three categories, 892 titles, 12,028 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 凡四部之錄四十五家，都管三千六十部，五萬一千八百五十二卷，成《書錄》四十卷。

translations.literal: In all, the Four Divisions register forty-five categories, altogether governing three thousand sixty titles and fifty-one thousand eight hundred fifty-two scrolls, forming the Bibliographic Record in forty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the Four Divisions register 45 categories, altogether governing 3,060 titles and 51,852 scrolls, forming the Bibliographic Record in 40 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其外有釋氏經律論疏，道家經戒符籙，凡二千五百餘部，九千五百餘卷。

translations.literal: Beyond these were Buddhist sutras, vinaya, treatises, and commentaries, and Daoist scriptures, precepts, talismans, and registers — more than two thousand five hundred titles and nine thousand five hundred scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these were Buddhist sutras, vinaya, treatises, and commentaries, and Daoist scriptures, precepts, talismans, and registers — more than 2,500 titles and 9,500 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 亦具翻譯名氏，序述指歸，又勒成目錄十卷，名曰《開元內外經錄》。

translations.literal: Translators' names were also fully given, prefaces and expositions set forth their purport, and a catalogue of ten scrolls was further compiled, titled Inner and Outer Scriptural Record of the Kaiyuan Era.
translations.idiomatic: Translators' names were also fully given, prefaces and expositions set forth their purport, and a catalogue of ten scrolls was further compiled, titled Inner and Outer Scriptural Record of the Kaiyuan Era.

sentences.zh: 若夫先王秘傳，列代奧文，自古之粹籍錄符，絕域之神經怪牒，盡載於此二書矣。

translations.literal: As for secret transmissions of former kings and profound writings of successive ages — choice compilations and talismanic records since antiquity, divine scriptures and strange documents from distant lands — all are fully loaded in these two books.
translations.idiomatic: As for secret transmissions of former kings and profound writings of successive ages — choice compilations and talismanic records since antiquity, divine scriptures and strange documents from distant lands — all are fully loaded in these two books.

sentences.zh: 夫經籍者，開物成務，垂教作程，聖哲之能事，帝王之達典。

translations.literal: Writings and records open things, accomplish tasks, hand down teaching, and establish standards — the able work of sages and the perfected canon of emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Writings and records open things, accomplish tasks, hand down teaching, and establish standards — the able work of sages and the perfected canon of emperors.

sentences.zh: 而去聖已久，開鑿遂多，苟不剖判條源，甄明科部，則先賢遺事，有卒代而不聞，大國經書，遂終年而空泯。

translations.literal: Yet the sages have long departed and excavations have grown many; if one does not divide sources by category and clarify divisions, then the legacy affairs of former worthies may pass a whole age unheard, and the classics of great states may vanish empty year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sages have long departed and excavations have grown many; if one does not divide sources by category and clarify divisions, then the legacy affairs of former worthies may pass a whole age unheard, and the classics of great states may vanish empty year after year.

sentences.zh: 使學者孤舟泳海，弱羽憑天，銜石填溟，倚杖追日，莫聞名目，豈詳家代？

translations.literal: It would make scholars a lone boat swimming the sea, weak wings relying on the sky, carrying stones to fill the ocean, leaning on a staff to chase the sun — never hearing titles, how could they know authors and ages?
translations.idiomatic: It would make scholars a lone boat swimming the sea, weak wings relying on the sky, carrying stones to fill the ocean, leaning on a staff to chase the sun — never hearing titles, how could they know authors and ages?

translations.literal: Is that not exhausting!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not exhausting!

translations.literal: Is that not ruinous!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not ruinous!

sentences.zh: 將使書千帙於掌眸，披萬函於年祀，覽錄而知旨，觀目而悉詞，經墳之精術盡探，賢哲之睿思鹹識，不見古人之面，而見古人之心，以傳後來，不其愈已！

translations.literal: It will let one hold a thousand bundles in the palm's glance and unfold ten thousand cases across the years; reading the catalogue one knows the purport, viewing entries one grasps the words — the refined arts of the canon fully explored, the keen thought of sages and worthies all understood: though one does not see the faces of the ancients, one sees their hearts — to transmit this to those who come after, is that not better still!
translations.idiomatic: It will let one hold a thousand bundles in the palm's glance and unfold ten thousand cases across the years; reading the catalogue one knows the purport, viewing entries one grasps the words — the refined arts of the canon fully explored, the keen thought of sages and worthies all understood: though one does not see the faces of the ancients, one sees their hearts — to transmit this to those who come after, is that not better still!

translations.literal: The preface is thus.
translations.idiomatic: The preface is thus.

sentences.zh: 煚等《四部目》及《釋道目》，並有小序及注撰人姓氏，卷軸繁多，今並略之，但紀篇部，以表我朝文物之大。

translations.literal: Jiong and others' Catalogue of the Four Divisions and Catalogue of Buddhist and Daoist Writings both had small prefaces and authors' surnames noted; scrolls were numerous — all are now omitted, recording only chapters and divisions to display the greatness of our dynasty's cultural achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and others' Catalogue of the Four Divisions and Catalogue of Buddhist and Daoist Writings both had small prefaces and authors' surnames noted; scrolls were numerous — all are now omitted, recording only chapters and divisions to display the greatness of our dynasty's cultural achievements.

sentences.zh: 其《釋道錄目》附本書，今亦不取，據開元以籍為之志。

translations.literal: The Buddhist and Daoist catalogue appended to this book is likewise not taken; we follow the Kaiyuan catalogue of writings for this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist and Daoist catalogue appended to this book is likewise not taken; we follow the Kaiyuan catalogue of writings for this treatise.

sentences.zh: 天寶已後，名公各著文章，儒者多有撰述，或記禮法之沿革，或裁國史之繁略，皆張部類，其徒實繁。

translations.literal: After the Tianbao era, eminent men each composed writings and Confucian scholars often produced treatises — some recording changes in ritual and law, others trimming the fullness or brevity of national history — all expanding their divisions; their number is truly great.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era, eminent men each composed writings and Confucian scholars often produced treatises — some recording changes in ritual and law, others trimming the fullness or brevity of national history — all expanding their divisions; their number is truly great.

sentences.zh: 臣以後出之書，在開元四部之外，不欲雜其本部，今據所聞，附撰人等傳。

translations.literal: I hold that books appearing later, outside the Kaiyuan Four Divisions, should not be mixed into their original divisions; according to what is known, they are appended to the biographies of their compilers.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that books appearing later, outside the Kaiyuan Four Divisions, should not be mixed into their original divisions; according to what is known, they are appended to the biographies of their compilers.

sentences.zh: 其諸公文集，亦見本傳，此並不錄。

translations.literal: The collected writings of various lords and ministers also appear in their own biographies; these are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The collected writings of various lords and ministers also appear in their own biographies; these are not recorded here.
